papers.title_en: Disentangled Fine-Grained Prototype Learning for Incomplete Image-Tabular Classification
papers.authors: Feixiang Zhou, Jianyang Xie, Zhuangzhi Gao, Qinkai Yu, Fu Wang, Yuheng Fan, Jing Li, Zheheng Jiang, Yitian Zhao, Yanda Meng, He Zhao, Gregory Y. H. Lip, Yalin Zheng
papers.evidence: 不完整多模态分类的解耦表示
papers.tldr: 图像-表格多模态学习面临缺失模态难题，现有方法仅基于全局特征进行粗粒度对齐，忽略细粒度语义与分布差异。本文提出DFPL框架，通过共享-特定原型建模提取紧凑原型，并利用原型引导的细粒度对齐保持分布与语义一致性，再以类别感知多尺度聚合自适应融合特征。在多个缺失模态设置下取得最优性能，展示了细粒度原型学习的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: The missing-modality problem poses a significant challenge in image-tabular multimodal learning across a wide range of multimedia applications, including product understanding, recommendation systems, and medical diagnosis. This challenge is particularly pronounced when the two modalities are highly heterogeneous, as images and tabular attributes differ substantially in their semantic granularity and data distributions. Existing methods learn modality-invariant representations through disentanglement and alignment over global token-averaged features, capturing only coarse cross-modal consistency and overlooking fine-grained semantic and distributional misalignment, which hampers the exploitation of complementary cues under missing modalities. To address this, we propose DFPL, a novel framework for fine-grained prototype learning. Specifically, Shared-Specific Prototype Modeling (SSPM) extracts compact and diverse shared and modality-specific prototypes, and further performs prototype-level disentanglement to suppress redundant intra-modality correlations. Additionally, we propose a Prototype-guided Fine-grained Alignment (PFA) module that jointly enforces prototype-level distribution matching and prototype-to-class semantic alignment within a unified prototype space, thereby preserving both fine-grained distributional and semantic consistency across modalities. We further introduce a Class-aware Multi-scale Aggregation (CMA) module to adaptively aggregate shared semantics and modality-specific characteristics from global and prototype levels for robust predictions. Extensive experiments on three diverse image-tabular benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method compared to the previous approaches under various missing-modality settings. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title_en: To Be Multimodal or Not to Be: Query-Adaptive Audio-Visual Person Retrieval via Active Modality Detection
papers.authors: Erfan Loweimi, Mengjie Qian, Kate Knill, Guanfeng Wu, Chi-Ho Chan, Abbas Haider, Muhammad Awan, Josef Kittler, Hui Wang, Mark Gales
papers.evidence: 主动模态检测处理音视频检索中的缺失模态
papers.tldr: 在真实广播视频中检索人物时，目标可能只出现在音频或视频中，固定多模态融合会因缺失模态的噪声而降低精度。本文提出查询自适应框架，利用跨模态分数一致性检测活跃模态，分类器准确率达89%。在BBC Rewind语料上，自适应系统P@1为94.2%，优于音频(82.9%)、视频(93.4%)和固定融合(90.0%)，恢复与理想系统(96.6%)差距的64%。该工作首次解决真实场景模态缺失问题，提升了检索鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: When retrieving a person from a video archive by voice and face, should the system be multimodal or not? In real-world broadcast archives, unlike curated benchmarks, a target may be heard but unseen, seen but unheard, or both. Fusing scores from an absent modality injects noise, degrading precision below the best unimodal system. We propose a query-adaptive framework that detects active modalities via cross-modal score consistency: when both modalities are active, files retrieved by one also score highly on the other; this agreement breaks down when a modality is absent. Classifiers driven by these cross-modal features achieve 89% detection accuracy. On the BBC Rewind corpus (with over 12,000 broadcast videos) the adaptive system attains 94.2% P@1, outperforming speaker-only (82.9%), face-only (93.4%), and fixed fusion (90.0%), recovering 64% of the gap to an oracle with ground-truth modality labels (96.6%).
